EVERQUEST

The World of Norrath

March 16, 1999 — Verant Interactive / Sony

Enter the World

The Story Begins

Every journey into Norrath opens with the same painted prologue — the story of the Gloomingdeep kobolds and the prisoner who carries a note. These are the original cinematic screens from the game, with the story text exactly as it appears in-game.

"The kobolds of Gloomingdeep dig far below the surface of Norrath. Greedy for treasure and the dark secrets of the depths, they recklessly expand their slave raids towards the nearby settlements of your homeland."
"Many have already been captured. Few have escaped. Fearing the further approach of the Gloomingdeep raiding parties,"
"your kindred have chosen you to journey to your home city and deliver a plea for help."
"As the gods would have it, you are captured long before you reach the capitol. Alone and far from home..."
"you find yourself beneath the lash of the Gloomingdeep Kobolds."
"You are relentlessly questioned about the note you were carrying. Regardless of your answers, the Kobolds pummel you between interrogations. As the hours pass, hope of survival fades. Soon you slip into unconsciousness."

Firiona Vie

The First Adventurer

Every adventure in EverQuest begins in the gloom of Gloomingdeep. The protagonist of the original game is Firiona Vie, a character created by lore master Bill Trost. When you first log in, you awaken as Firiona Vie — a prisoner of the Gloomingdeep kobolds, carrying a plea for help from her homeland. The cinematic above is her story, and it is your story: the note she was carrying becomes the first quest of a campaign that will span the whole of Norrath.

Fourteen Paths

EverQuest launched in 1999 with fourteen playable classes, each tied to specific races. Two more — the Beastlord and the Berserker — joined in later expansions.

Melee

Warrior

A tank-based character in heavy armor, designed to take damage for its group using a taunt ability.

Monk

A fighter who uses a combination of martial arts and barehanded fighting techniques.

Rogue

A combination of thief and assassin who can sneak and hide in the shadows as well as steal from enemies.

Priest

Cleric

A heavily specialized support class that wears heavy armor and is adept at healing and strengthening allies.

Druid

A magic-user who draws power from nature, able to restore the vitality and magic power of teammates.

Shaman

A tribal warrior who draws upon the spirit realm to heal and empower allies, and to weaken enemies.

Casters

Wizard

A specialized damage-dealer wielding fire, ice, and pure magic energy, with teleportation abilities.

Magician

A summoner who calls upon elemental servants to aid in dealing damage.

Necromancer

A dark caster who uses disease and poison to wither opponents while commanding undead allies.

Enchanter

An illusionist who can take on many forms, strengthen allies with spells, and pacify enemies with mesmerizing abilities.

Hybrids

Paladin

A knight who can take damage or heal with magic and the laying on of hands.

Shadowknight

A dark warrior combining melee attacks with disease and poison, able to take damage for the party.

Bard

A minstrel whose magical songs damage enemies, strengthen allies, and improve the movement speed of herself and others.

Ranger

A protector of nature with healing and support magic, who fights at close range or with bows and arrows — and can track her quarry.

Added in Later Expansions

Beastlord — Shadows of Luclin (2001)

A primal fighter constantly joined by animal wards that help deal damage, who also assists teammates with healing and support skills.

Berserker — Gates of Discord (2004)

A strong fighter specializing in two-handed weapons such as axes, able to enter a state of increased fury and power.

The Peoples of Norrath

Sixteen playable races, split between the factions of Good and Evil — with Neutral races free to choose either path. Each race carries its own starting city, racial traits, and roster of classes.

A World of Over 500 Zones

The world of Norrath is divided into more than five hundred zones representing plains, oceans, cities, deserts, and other planes of existence. A few landmarks:

The Plane of Knowledge

One of the most popular zones in the game — one of the few where all races and classes coexist harmoniously. It serves as a hub of portals to other planes and to the outskirts of nearly every starting city.

Oasis of Marr

A desert zone where sand giants roam the dunes — one of the many harsh landscapes the world of Norrath is built from.

Freeport

The human starting city, where human characters begin their journeys and where the first steps of the game's story unfold. It sits on the eastern end of Antonica, opposite the western city of Qeynos — the two great homes of the humans.

Felwithe & Kelethin

The elven starting lands — high elves set out from Felwithe, while wood elves begin their journeys in Kelethin.

How It Played

The systems that defined a genre

Character Creation
At creation you choose an adventuring occupation (your class), a patron deity, a starting city, and customize your face — hair, facial features, and eyes. Some classes are restricted to particular races.
Group Roles
Every class has a distinct role in a group, and classes were designed to complement one another. Group leaders assign roles — Leader, Main Tank, Main Assist, Puller — directly in the group window.
Quests & Valor
NPCs hand out quests that drive the story, and valorous deeds — reclaiming overrun castles, defeating worthy opponents — earn lasting rewards.
Guilds & Raids
EverQuest was the first MMORPG to feature a full guild system and raids — one of the reasons the GDC placed it in its Hall of Fame in 2011.
PvP
Dedicated PvP servers, arena zones, and consensual duels let players settle scores — the rules of engagement varied by server and zone.
Living Worlds
Over 500 zones across multiple continents, each server holding thousands of players — at peak, 3,000+ adventurers roamed a single server at once.

From MUD to Legend

1996
John Smedley, an executive at Sony's Interactive Studios America, secures funding for a 3D game in the spirit of text-based MUDs, following the success of Meridian 59. He hires programmers Brad McQuaid and Steve Clover, while Bill Trost creates the history, lore, and major characters of Norrath.
November 1997
Brad McQuaid announces the start of beta testing.
March 16, 1999
EverQuest launches under Verant Interactive with a budget of $15 million. It becomes one of the first MMORPGs to support 3D graphics and a full 360° field of view. The game sells 10,000 subscriptions in its first 24 hours and reaches 60,000 by April 1999.
1999
By the end of the year, EverQuest has surpassed Ultima Online in subscriptions, becoming the best-selling MMORPG of its time. It is named 1999 Game of the Year by GameSpot.
2000
Sony reorganizes Verant Interactive into Sony Online Entertainment. The first expansion, The Ruins of Kunark, releases on April 24, raising the level cap to 60.
2001
Shadows of Luclin (December 4) adds the Beastlord class and a character model facelift.
2002
Planes of Power (October 29) introduces the Plane of Knowledge hub. The New Dawn version launches on European servers.
2003
The Mac OS X version of EverQuest releases (June 24). Digital distribution begins with Legacy of Ykesha.
2004
Gates of Discord (February 10) adds the Berserker class and the Drakkin race. EverQuest II releases in November, while EverQuest continues its own storyline.
2007
SOE wins a Technology & Engineering Emmy Award for its work in MMO development.
2012
EverQuest goes free-to-play with Bronze, Silver, and Gold subscription tiers (March).
2015
SOE is sold off and becomes Daybreak Game Company.
2025
The 32nd expansion, Shattering of Ro, releases on December 2, raising the level cap to 130.

Thirty-Two Expansions

Two and a half decades of content

The first four expansions arrived in physical boxes at roughly one-year intervals — huge new landmasses, new playable races, new classes. From 2003 onward the pace quickened to two a year, then settled to one. Buying the latest expansion unlocks every one before it.

Servers Named for the Gods

A world of communities

Shards of Norrath
Every EverQuest server carries a unique name drawn from the deities of Norrath. Characters are locked to their server — transfers are possible, but arranged through customer service, usually for a fee. Each server grew its own community, and players often wear their server name as part of their identity.
Al'Kabor
The dedicated Mac OS X server, opened in June 2003 and closed in November 2013. SOE split it from an early Planes of Power build, so it carried features and bugs never seen on the PC servers.
European Shores
Antonius Bayle and Kane Bayle anchored European play; Kane later merged into Antonius. Under the New Dawn promotion, Ubisoft ran Venril Sathir (Britain), Sebilis (France), and Kael Drakkal (Germany), all since folded into Antonius Bayle.
Project 1999
Unofficial servers that recreate EverQuest as it was at launch — the original game plus the first two expansions, the "Classic Trilogy." A living museum of the 1999 world.

"The EQ button lists many shortcuts to windows and other useful commands."
"Caster classes can right-click an empty spell gem to choose a spell to scribe."

"Group leaders can assign roles to group members by right-clicking on their name in the group window."
